questions.question: A man receives ₹9475 per month as salary. He saves 88% of his salary every month. His expenditure per month is:2163
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total Salary = 100%

Expenditure % = 100% − Savings % = 100% − 88% = 12%

Expenditure = 12% of Total Salary

Expenditure = (12 × 9475) ÷ 100

Expenditure = 113700 ÷ 100 = 1137

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1137.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total Monthly Salary = ₹9475

Monthly Savings = 88% of Salary

 
 
 
 Savings (88%)
 Exp.

 

 Total Salary = ₹9475 (100%)
 
 

 12% = ?

**Formula Used:**

Expenditure % = 100% − Savings %

Expenditure Amount = (Expenditure % ÷ 100) × Total Salary

**Calculations:**

⇒ Expenditure % = 100% − 88%

⇒ Expenditure % = 12%

⇒ Expenditure Amount = (12 ÷ 100) × 9475

⇒ Expenditure Amount = 12 × 94.75

⇒ Expenditure Amount = 1137

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1137.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Income & Expenditure Principle

Total Income is always considered as the 100% base. Since Income = Savings + Expenditure, any change in percentage distribution directly affects the actual amounts proportionally.

Successive Percentage Change

If a value changes successively by a% and b%, the effective percentage change is calculated as a + b + (a × b) ÷ 100.

Percentage Change Formula

The percentage change between an old and a new value is defined as: Percentage Change = (New Value − Original Value) ÷ Original Value × 100.

questions.question: {Find the value of } tan 10circ tan 18circ tan 72circ tan 80circ
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

If A + B = 90°, then tan A × tan B = 1.

We can pair the complementary angles: (tan 10° × tan 80°) × (tan 18° × tan 72°).

Since 10° + 80° = 90°, the product of the first pair is 1.

Since 18° + 72° = 90°, the product of the second pair is also 1.

Total product = 1 × 1 = 1.

**∴ The correct answer is 1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Expression: tan 10° × tan 18° × tan 72° × tan 80°

**Formula Used:**

tan(90° − θ) = cot θ

tan θ × cot θ = 1

**Calculation:**

⇒ tan 10° × tan 18° × tan 72° × tan 80°

⇒ tan 10° × tan 18° × tan(90° − 18°) × tan(90° − 10°)

⇒ tan 10° × tan 18° × cot 18° × cot 10°

Rearranging the terms to group complementary pairs:

⇒ (tan 10° × cot 10°) × (tan 18° × cot 18°)

Applying the reciprocal identity tan θ × cot θ = 1:

⇒ 1 × 1

⇒ 1

**∴ The correct answer is 1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Complementary Angles

Two angles are complementary if their sum is exactly 90°. Trigonometric co-functions are equal for such pairs, meaning sin(90° − θ) = cos θ and tan(90° − θ) = cot θ.

Reciprocal Identities

The product of any standard trigonometric ratio and its mathematical reciprocal is always 1. Thus, tan θ × cot θ = 1, sin θ × cosec θ = 1, and cos θ × sec θ = 1.
</p

questions.question: The amount on a sum of ₹9,400 at 20% per annum compound interest, compounded annually, in 2 years will be:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Effective compound interest rate for 2 years at 20% p.a. = 20 + 20 + (20 × 20) ÷ 100 = 44%

Total Amount = Principal (100%) + Interest (44%) = 144%

Amount = 144% of 9400 = 1.44 × 9400

⇒ Amount = 13536

Principal (P) = ₹9400

Rate (R) = 20% per annum

Time (n) = 2 years

**Formula Used:**

Amount (A) = P × (1 + R/100)ⁿ

**Calculations:**

⇒ A = 9400 × (1 + 1/5)²

Effective Rate of Compound Interest

For 2 years at a rate of R%, the effective compound interest rate can be found directly using the net change formula: (R + R + R×R ÷ 100)%.

Compound Interest Formula (Half-Yearly)

When interest is compounded half-yearly, the rate is halved (R/2) and the time periods are doubled (2n). The formula becomes: A = P(1 + R/200)²ⁿ.

SI vs CI Difference for 2 Years

The exact difference between compound interest and simple interest on a principal for 2 years is calculated using the formula: Difference = P × (R/100)².

questions.question: The sum of the first pair of two-digit twin prime numbers is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Twin primes are prime numbers that differ by exactly 2.

The smallest two-digit prime numbers are 11 and 13.

Since 13 − 11 = 2, they form the first two-digit twin prime pair.

Sum = 11 + 13 = 24.

**∴ The correct answer is 24.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

We need to find the sum of the first pair of two-digit twin prime numbers.

**Concept Used:**

**Prime Number:** A natural number greater than 1 that has exactly two distinct divisors: 1 and itself.

**Twin Primes:** A pair of prime numbers that have a difference of exactly 2.

**Calculations:**

⇒ The two-digit prime numbers starting from the smallest are: 11, 13, 17, 19, 23, 29, 31, ...

⇒ Let us find the first pair with a difference of 2.

⇒ 13 − 11 = 2

⇒ Thus, the first pair of two-digit twin prime numbers is (11, 13).

⇒ The sum of this prime pair = 11 + 13 = 24.

**∴ The correct answer is 24.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Prime Numbers

Numbers that have exactly two distinct factors: 1 and the number itself. The smallest prime number is 2, which is also the only even prime number.

Co-prime Numbers

Two numbers are co-prime if their highest common factor (HCF) is 1. They do not necessarily need to be prime numbers individually (e.g., 8 and 15 are co-prime).

Composite Numbers

Numbers that have more than two factors. The smallest composite number is 4. Note that 1 is neither a prime nor a composite number.
</p

questions.question: The cost of 2 chocolates and 3 cookies is ₹ 36. The cost of 1 chocolate and 2 cookies is ₹ 23. What is the cost of 4 chocolates and 5 cookies?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let 1 Chocolate = C and 1 Cookie = K.

Given: 2C + 3K = 36 and 1C + 2K = 23

We need to find the total cost of 4C + 5K.

Observe the direct pattern: 3 × (2C + 3K) − 2 × (1C + 2K) = 6C + 9K − 2C − 4K = 4C + 5K

Required Cost = 3 × 36 − 2 × 23 = 108 − 46 = 62

**∴ The correct answer is ₹ 62.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 
 2 Choco + 3 Cookies
 = ₹ 36

 
 1 Choco + 2 Cookies
 = ₹ 23

 
• 

 
 4 Choco + 5 Cookies
 = ₹ 62

**Given:**

Cost of 2 chocolates and 3 cookies = ₹ 36

Cost of 1 chocolate and 2 cookies = ₹ 23

**Method Used:**

Let the cost of 1 chocolate be x and 1 cookie be y.

Set up linear equations in two variables and solve algebraically.

**Calculations:**

⇒ 2x + 3y = 36 — (Equation 1)

⇒ x + 2y = 23 — (Equation 2)

⇒ Multiplying Equation 2 by 2, we get:

⇒ 2x + 4y = 46 — (Equation 3)

⇒ Subtracting Equation 1 from Equation 3:

⇒ (2x + 4y) − (2x + 3y) = 46 − 36

⇒ y = 10

⇒ Substituting y = 10 in Equation 2:

⇒ x + 2(10) = 23

⇒ x + 20 = 23

⇒ x = 3

⇒ The cost of 4 chocolates and 5 cookies = 4x + 5y

⇒ Total Cost = 4(3) + 5(10)

⇒ Total Cost = 12 + 50 = 62

**∴ The correct answer is ₹ 62.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Linear Equations in Two Variables

Mathematical expressions of the form ax + by = c. They can be solved algebraically using substitution or elimination methods to find the specific values of unknown quantities.

Elimination Method

This involves multiplying one or both equations by suitable constants so that the coefficients of one variable become equal, then adding or subtracting the equations to eliminate it.

Substitution Method

An alternative technique where you find the value of one variable in terms of the other from the first equation and substitute it into the second equation.

questions.question:
Simplify the following.
 (3x² + 4x²) div 7x
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Apply BODMAS directly by adding like terms first, then dividing:

⇒ (3x² + 4x²) ÷ 7x

⇒ 7x² ÷ 7x

⇒ x

**∴ The correct answer is x.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Expression: (3x² + 4x²) ÷ 7x

**Formula Used:**

Addition of like terms: axⁿ + bxⁿ = (a + b)xⁿ

Law of exponents for division: am ÷ aⁿ = am−ⁿ

**Calculations:**

⇒ According to the BODMAS rule, solve the bracket first.

⇒ 3x² + 4x² = 7x²

⇒ Now, divide the result by 7x.

⇒ 7x² ÷ 7x = (7 ÷ 7) × (x² ÷ x¹)

⇒ 1 × x²−¹

⇒ x

**∴ The correct answer is x.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

BODMAS Rule

It stands for Bracket, Of, Division, Multiplication, Addition, and Subtraction. Always solve expressions inside parentheses first.

Law of Exponents (Multiplication)

When multiplying expressions with the same base, add the exponents: am × aⁿ = am⁺ⁿ

Law of Exponents (Division)

When dividing expressions with the same base, subtract the exponents: am ÷ aⁿ = am−ⁿ
</p

questions.question: An item is sold for ₹8,900 after two successive discounts of 20% and 11%. What is the marked price (in ₹) of the item?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

By using the fractional multiplier method for successive percentages:

20% = 1/5 ⇒ Multiplier = 4/5

11% = 11/100 ⇒ Multiplier = 89/100

MP × 4/5 × 89/100 = 8900

MP = 8900 × 5/4 × 100/89 = 12500

**∴ The correct answer is ₹12,500.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Final Selling Price (SP) = ₹8,900

First successive discount (D₁) = 20%

Second successive discount (D₂) = 11%

**Formula Used:**

SP = MP × (100 − D₁)/100 × (100 − D₂)/100

 
 
 
 

 
 

 
 
 
 
 
 
 
• 
 
• 
 
 
 MP = ?
 SP1
 ₹ 8900
 
 
 - 20%
 - 11%
 
 Successive Discounts Progression

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the initial Marked Price be MP.

⇒ 8900 = MP × (100 − 20)/100 × (100 − 11)/100

⇒ 8900 = MP × 80/100 × 89/100

⇒ 8900 = MP × 4/5 × 89/100

⇒ MP = 8900 × 5/4 × 100/89

⇒ MP = 100 × 5/4 × 100

⇒ MP = 125 × 100

⇒ MP = 12500

**∴ The correct answer is ₹12,500.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Marked Price (MP)

The price printed on an article or item. Discounts are fundamentally always calculated on the marked price.

Successive Discounts

When two consecutive discounts d₁% and d₂% are given, the single equivalent net discount percentage is calculated as (d₁ + d₂ − d₁×d₂/100)%.

Selling Price (SP)

The final transaction price at which an item is sold after all the sequential discounts are deducted. SP = MP − Total Discount.

questions.question:
The present age of a father is 4 times the age of his daughter. Five years ago, the father was 7 times as old as his daughter. 
What is the present age of the daughter?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Present ratio of Father : Daughter = 4 : 1 (Difference = 3 parts)

Ratio 5 years ago = 7 : 1 (Difference = 6 parts)

To make the age difference constant, multiply the present ratio by 2 → New present ratio = 8 : 2

Decrease in ratio parts for both = 8 − 7 = 1 part, and 2 − 1 = 1 part.

1 part corresponds to 5 years, so present age of daughter = 2 parts × 5 = 10 years.

**∴ The correct answer is 10 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

⇒ Present age of father is 4 times the daughter's age.

⇒ 5 years ago, father was 7 times as old as the daughter.

questions.question: A and B started moving at the same time towards each other from points X and Y, respectively. After meeting on the way, A and B took 95.4 hours and p hours, respectively, to reach Y and X, respectively. If the speed of B is 50% more than that of A, then what is the value of p?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For objects moving towards each other, the speed ratio is the inverse square root of their times taken to reach destinations after meeting.

Speed ratio (vA / vB) = 1 / 1.5 = 2 / 3

Time ratio equation: vA / vB = √(tB / tA)

Squaring both sides: (2 / 3)² = p / 95.4

p = (4 ÷ 9) × 95.4 = 42.4

**∴ The correct answer is p = 42.4.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by A after meeting to reach Y, tA = 95.4 hours

Time taken by B after meeting to reach X, tB = p hours

Speed of B is 50% more than that of A.

⇒ Let speed of A (vA) = 2x, then speed of B (vB) = 3x.

⇒ Ratio of speeds, vA / vB = 2x / 3x = 2 / 3<

questions.question: If 66 is the mean proportion between x and 99, what is the value of x?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The mean proportion of two numbers a and c is given by √(a × c).

Given the mean proportion is 66, and the numbers are x and 99.

So, 66² = x × 99

x = (66 × 66) ÷ 99 = 4356 ÷ 99 = 44

**∴ The correct answer is 44.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Mean proportion (b) = 66

First term (a) = x

Third term (c) = 99

**Formula Used:**

If a, b, and c are in continued proportion, then b² = a × c

 
 

 Product of Extremes (x × 99)

 :

 
 99

 
 

 Product of Means (66 × 66)

 
 99x = 4356 ⇒ x = 44

**Calculations:**

⇒ b² = a × c

⇒ 66² = x × 99

⇒ 4356 = 99x

⇒ x = 4356 ÷ 99

⇒ x = 44

**∴ The correct answer is 44.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Third Proportion

If a, b, and c are in continued proportion, then c is called the third proportional to a and b. Formula: c = b² ÷ a.

Fourth Proportion

If a : b :: c : d, then d is called the fourth proportional to a, b, and c. Formula: d = (b × c) ÷ a.

Duplicate & Sub-duplicate Ratios

The duplicate ratio of a : b is a² : b². The sub-duplicate ratio of a : b is √a : √b.
</p

questions.question: In an election with three candidates, M, N and R, candidate M secured 42% of the total votes, while candidate R obtained 34%. If the total number of votes polled was 37,700 and all were valid, how many votes did candidate N receive?

questions.question: Rishi can do a piece of work in 12 days. Shan is 20% more efficient than Rishi. The number of days taken by Shan to do the same piece of work is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Efficiency ratio of Rishi to Shan = 100 : 120 = 5 : 6

Time is inversely proportional to efficiency, so Time ratio = 6 : 5

6 units of time = 12 days (Time taken by Rishi)

1 unit of time = 12 ÷ 6 = 2 days

Shan's time (5 units) = 5 × 2 = 10 days

**∴ The correct answer is 10 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by Rishi to complete the work = 12 days

Shan is 20% more efficient than Rishi.

**Formula Used:**

Total Work = Efficiency × Time

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let Rishi's efficiency be 5 units/day.

⇒ Shan's efficiency = 120% of 5 = (120 ÷ 100) × 5 = 6 units/day.

⇒ Total Work = Rishi's efficiency × Rishi's days = 5 × 12 = 60 units.

 
 

 **Person**
 **Days**
 **Total Work**
 **Efficiency**
 
 

 Rishi
 12
 60
 5
 
 

 Shan
 10
 6
 
 

⇒ Time taken by Shan = Total Work ÷ Shan's efficiency

⇒ Time taken by Shan = 60 ÷ 6 = 10 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 10 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Efficiency and Time Relationship

Time taken to complete a work is inversely proportional to efficiency. If the efficiency ratio of two persons is a : b, their time ratio to complete the same work will be b : a.

Total Work Rule

Total Work = Efficiency × Time. Since total work remains constant, any increase in efficiency leads to a proportional decrease in time required.

Combined Work Concept

If two individuals work together, their combined efficiency is the sum of their individual efficiencies. Combined Time = Total Work ÷ (Efficiency A + Efficiency B).
</p

questions.question: A rectangular water tank 5 m long and 3 m wide contains water up to a depth of 1.50 m. The area of the wet surface is:

The wet surface area is the sum of the tank's base area and the lateral surface area (4 walls) up to the water depth.

Wet Area = (l × b) + 2h(l + b)

⇒ Wet Area = 15 + 3 × 8

⇒ Wet Area = 15 + 24 = 39 m²

questions.question: A table is bought for ₹1,400 and sold at a loss of 6%. Find its selling price.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Since the loss is 6%, the selling price is (100 − 6)% = 94% of the cost price.

SP = 94% of CP

SP = (94 ÷ 100) × 1400

SP = 94 × 14 = 1316

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1,316.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 
 CP = ₹1400
 
 
 SP = ?
 
 
• 
 

 
 Loss: 6%
 - ₹84

**Given:**

Cost Price (CP) of the table = ₹1,400

Loss percentage = 6%

**Formula Used:**

Loss amount = CP × (Loss% ÷ 100)

Selling Price (SP) = CP − Loss amount

**Calculations:**

⇒ Loss amount = 1400 × (6 ÷ 100)

⇒ Loss amount = 14 × 6

⇒ Loss amount = ₹84

⇒ Selling Price (SP) = 1400 − 84

⇒ Selling Price (SP) = ₹1,316

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1,316.**

questions.question:
What is the mode of the following data?

65, 86, 86, 85, 69, 90, 71, 60, 86, 71, 86, 65, 81, 82, 67, 72, 84, 66, 75, 85, 68, 78, 61, 64, 74, 90
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The mode of a given dataset is simply the value that appears most frequently.

By quickly observing the numbers, we can see that 86 is repeated the maximum number of times.

Frequency of 86 = 4 times (which is the highest).

**∴ The correct answer is 86.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Data: 65, 86, 86, 85, 69, 90, 71, 60, 86, 71, 86, 65, 81, 82, 67, 72, 84, 66, 75, 85, 68, 78, 61, 64, 74, 90

**Formula Used:**

Mode = Value with the highest frequency in the dataset.

**Calculation:**

⇒ Let us count the frequency of each distinct value in the data.

⇒ 60 → 1, 61 → 1, 64 → 1, 65 → 2

⇒ 66 → 1, 67 → 1, 68 → 1, 69 → 1

⇒ 71 → 2, 72 → 1, 74 → 1, 75 → 1

⇒ 78 → 1, 81 → 1, 82 → 1, 84 → 1

⇒ 85 → 2, 86 → 4, 90 → 2

⇒ Comparing the frequencies, the number 86 has the maximum frequency of 4.

**∴ The correct answer is 86.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Mean

The mean is the average of all the numbers in a data set, calculated as the sum of all observations divided by the total number of observations.

Median

The median is the middle value of a sorted data set. If the number of observations is even, it is the average of the two middle numbers.

Empirical Formula

The relationship between mean, median, and mode for a moderately skewed distribution is given by: Mode = 3 × Median − 2 × Mean.

Range

The range of a data set is the difference between the highest and lowest values in the dataset (Range = Maximum value − Minimum value).
</p

questions.question: The speed of a train 200 m long is 50 km/hr. How much time will it take to pass a platform 600 m long?

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total distance covered = Train length + Platform length = 200 + 600 = 800 m.

Speed in m/s = 50 × (5/18) = 125/9 m/s.

Time = Distance ÷ Speed = 800 × (9/125) = 57.6 sec.

**∴ The correct answer is 57.6 sec.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Length of train = 200 m

Length of platform = 600 m

Speed of train = 50 km/hr

**Formula Used:**

Time = Total Distance ÷ Speed

Speed in m/s = Speed in km/hr × (5/18)

 
 Train 200m

• 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total Distance = Length of train + Length of platform

⇒ Total Distance = 200 + 600 = 800 m

⇒ Speed in m/s = 50 × (5/18) = 125/9 m/s

⇒ Time taken = 800 ÷ (125/9)

⇒ Time taken = (800 × 9) ÷ 125

Conversion of Speeds

To convert km/hr to m/s, multiply the value by 5/18. To convert m/s to km/hr, multiply the value by 18/5.

Train Crossing a Stationary Point Object

When a train crosses a pole, standing man, or a tree, the total distance covered to clear the object is exactly equal to the length of the train itself.

Train Crossing an Extended Object

When a train crosses a platform, a bridge, or another stationary train, the total distance covered is the sum of the length of the train and the length of the extended object.

questions.question: A shopkeeper fixed the marked price of an article as ₹2,40,000. He gave 30% and 18% successive discounts on one article and 48% discount on another article of the same marked price. On which of the two articles did the shopkeeper get more benefit and how much more was it?

questions.question: If the mode of a data exceeds its mean by 34.8, then the mode exceeds the median by _____. (Use empirical formula to find the answer)4233

From the empirical relationship, the difference between Mode and Median is exactly two-thirds of the difference between Mode and Mean.

Mode − Median = ²/₃ × (Mode − Mean)

Mode − Median = ²/₃ × 34.8

Mode − Median = 2 × 11.6 = 23.2

Empirical Formula for a moderately skewed distribution:

⇒ Mode = 3 Median − 2 Mean

Subtracting Mean from both sides:

⇒ Mode − Mean = 3 Median − 3 Mean

⇒ Mode − Mean = 3 × (Median − Mean)

Substitute the given value:

⇒ 34.8 = 3 × (Median − Mean)

⇒ Median − Mean = 11.6

Empirical Relationship Formula

For a moderately skewed frequency distribution, the central tendencies are connected by the rule: Mode = 3 × Median − 2 × Mean.

Symmetrical Distribution

In a perfectly symmetrical or normal distribution curve, the Mean, Median, and Mode perfectly coincide at the center point.

Skewed Distribution Order

In a positively skewed distribution, the sequence follows Mean > Median > Mode. Conversely, in a negatively skewed distribution, it follows Mean < Median < Mode.

questions.question: Pipe A can fill a tank in 33 minutes and Pipe B can fill it in 22 minutes. Pipe C empties it. If all of the pipes are opened together, the tank will be full in 55 minutes. In how many minutes will pipe C empty the full tank?3083
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total capacity of the tank = LCM(33, 22, 55) = 330 units.

Efficiency of A = 330 ÷ 33 = 10 units/min.

Efficiency of B = 330 ÷ 22 = 15 units/min.

Combined efficiency (A + B − C) = 330 ÷ 55 = 6 units/min.

Efficiency of C = (10 + 15) − 6 = 19 units/min.

**∴ The correct answer is 17⁷/₁₉ minutes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by Pipe A to fill the tank = 33 minutes

Time taken by Pipe B to fill the tank = 22 minutes

Time taken by all pipes A, B, and C together to fill the tank = 55 minutes

**Formula Used:**

Total Work = Efficiency × Time

 
 

 **Pipe**
 **Minutes**
 **Total Work**
 **Efficiency**
 
 

 A

 330
 330 ÷ 33 = 10
 
 

 B

 330 ÷ 22 = 15

 330 ÷ 55 = 6
 
 

⇒ Combined Efficiency of A + B − C = 6

⇒ 10 + 15 − C = 6

⇒ 25 − C = 6

⇒ C = 25 − 6 = 19 units/min

⇒ Time taken by C to empty the tank = Total Work ÷ Efficiency of C

⇒ Time = 330 ÷ 19 = 17⁷/₁₉ minutes

**∴ The correct answer is 17⁷/₁₉ minutes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Pipes and Cisterns Basics

A filling pipe contributes positive work (+), while an emptying pipe (leak or outlet) contributes negative work (−) to the system.

Net Work Principle

If Pipe A fills the tank in x minutes and Pipe B empties it in y minutes, their combined net work in 1 minute is (1/x − 1/y). The tank fills if the net value is positive and empties if negative.

LCM Method for Total Capacity

Taking the Least Common Multiple (LCM) of the given times provides an assumed "Total Capacity" in units, making it easy to calculate individual efficiencies without dealing with complex fractions.
</p

questions.question: Simplify: sqrt{121 times 49} + sqrt{64 times 36} - sqrt{100 times 16}
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

We can separate the square roots directly using the property √(a × b) = √a × √b:

⇒ (11 × 7) + (8 × 6) − (10 × 4)

⇒ 77 + 48 − 40

⇒ 125 − 40 = 85

**∴ The correct answer is 85.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Expression: √(121 × 49) + √(64 × 36) − √(100 × 16)

**Formula Used:**

√(x × y) = √x × √y

**Calculation:**

⇒ √(121 × 49) = √121 × √49 = 11 × 7 = 77

⇒ √(64 × 36) = √64 × √36 = 8 × 6 = 48

⇒ √(100 × 16) = √100 × √16 = 10 × 4 = 40

Substituting the calculated values back into the main expression:

⇒ 77 + 48 − 40

⇒ 125 − 40

⇒ 85

**∴ The correct answer is 85.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

BODMAS Rule

Always follow the strict sequence of Brackets, Order (Powers/Roots), Division/Multiplication, and Addition/Subtraction from left to right to ensure an accurate result.

Properties of Radicals

The product of two square roots is equivalent to the square root of their product: √a × √b = √(a × b). This property is universally valid for all non-negative real numbers.

Common Perfect Squares

Memorizing squares up to 30 heavily aids in faster calculation during simplification questions (e.g., 11² = 121, 15² = 225, 25² = 625).
</p

questions.question: What is the smallest natural number that should be added to 9054 such that a remainder of 6 is left when the resulting number is divided by each of the numbers 28, 24, 56 and 29?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

LCM(28, 24, 56, 29) = 4872.

The resulting number must be of the general form (4872k + 6) to leave a remainder of 6.

To strictly exceed the base number 9054, we choose k = 2, which gives 4872 × 2 + 6 = 9750.

Smallest number to be added = 9750 − 9054 = 696.

**∴ The correct answer is 696.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Divisors: 28, 24, 56, and 29

Base number = 9054

Required remainder = 6

**Formula Used:**

Resulting Number = (LCM of divisors × k) + Remainder

**Calculations:**

⇒ Prime factorization of 28 = 2² × 7

⇒ Prime factorization of 24 = 2³ × 3

⇒ Prime factorization of 56 = 2³ × 7

⇒ Prime factorization of 29 = 29 × 1

⇒ LCM(28, 24, 56, 29) = 2³ × 3 × 7 × 29 = 8 × 3 × 7 × 29 = 4872

⇒ The resulting number must be of the form: (4872k + 6)

⇒ We need a multiple of 4872 that makes the result greater than 9054.

⇒ For k = 1, Result = 4872 × 1 + 6 = 4878 (which is less than 9054)

⇒ For k = 2, Result = 4872 × 2 + 6 = 9744 + 6 = 9750

⇒ Let the smallest natural number added be x.

⇒ 9054 + x = 9750

⇒ x = 9750 − 9054 = 696

**∴ The correct answer is 696.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

LCM with Same Remainder

When a number is divided by a, b, and c leaving the same remainder r in each case, the general form of the number is LCM(a, b, c)k + r.

LCM with Different Remainders

When a number is divided by a, b, and c leaving remainders x, y, and z respectively, and the common difference R = (a − x) = (b − y) = (c − z), the number is of the form LCM(a, b, c)k − R.

HCF with Same Remainder

The greatest number that divides x, y, and z leaving the same remainder r in each case is found by calculating HCF((x − r), (y − r), (z − r)).
</p

questions.question: The expenditure of Sudha is 100% more than her savings. If her expenditure decreases by 4% and savings increase by 35%, then by what percent does her income increase?4736
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Using the Weighted Average method for Percentage Change:

Expenditure is 100% more than Savings ⇒ Ratio of Expenditure : Savings = 2 : 1

Net % change in Income = [(Ratio of Exp × % Change in Exp) + (Ratio of Sav × % Change in Sav)] ÷ (Total Ratio)

Net % change = [2 × (−4) + 1 × 35] ÷ (2 + 1) = (−8 + 35) ÷ 3

Net % change = 27 ÷ 3 = +9%

**∴ The correct answer is 9%.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Expenditure is 100% more than Savings.

 Initial State: Income = 300
 
 
 Exp = 200
 Sav = 100
 
 Final State: Income = 327
 
 
 Exp = 192 (−4%)
 Sav = 135 (+35%)
 
 
• 
 
• 
 

 +27

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let initial Savings = 100

⇒ Initial Expenditure = 100 + 100% of 100 = 200

⇒ Initial Income = Expenditure + Savings = 200 + 100 = 300

⇒ New Expenditure = 200 − 4% of 200 = 200 − 8 = 192

⇒ New Savings = 100 + 35% of 100 = 100 + 35 = 135

⇒ New Income = New Expenditure + New Savings = 192 + 135 = 327

⇒ Increase in Income = 327 − 300 = 27

⇒ Percentage Increase = (Increase ÷ Initial Income) × 100

⇒ Percentage Increase = (27 ÷ 300) × 100 = 9%

**∴ The correct answer is 9%.**

**__Additional Information__**

Income, Expenditure & Savings

Income is always the sum of Expenditure and Savings. Income = Expenditure + Savings. Any absolute change in income equals the sum of absolute changes in expenditure and savings.

Weighted Average Method for Percentages

When a quantity is divided into parts in the ratio a : b, and the parts change by x% and y% respectively, the net percentage change of the total quantity is given by (ax + by) ÷ (a + b).

Percentage Change

Percentage Change = [(Final Value − Initial Value) ÷ Initial Value] × 100. A positive result indicates an increase, while a negative result indicates a decrease.
</p

questions.question: The area of a rectangle gets reduced by 21 m² if its length is reduced by 7 m and breadth is increased by 5 m and if its length is increased by 4 m and breadth is increased by 5 m, the area is increased by 67 m². Find the original area of the rectangle.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In both conditions, the new breadth is the same (B + 5), so the area difference is purely due to length.

Difference in new lengths = (L + 4) − (L − 7) = 11 m.

Difference in area = (A + 67) − (A − 21) = 88 m².

So, 11 × (B + 5) = 88 ⇒ B + 5 = 8 ⇒ B = 3 m.

Using Condition 1 Area: (L − 7) × 8 = 3L − 21 ⇒ 5L = 35 ⇒ L = 7 m.

**∴ The correct answer is 21 m².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 
 
 Area = A
 Length = L
 Breadth = B
 
 
 
 A − 21
 L − 7
 B + 5
 
 
 
 A + 67
 L + 4
 B + 5

**Given:**

⇒ Let the original length be L and breadth be B.

⇒ Original area (A) = L × B

**Case 1:** Length is reduced by 7 m and breadth is increased by 5 m.

⇒ New Area = (L − 7)(B + 5)

⇒ LB − 21 = LB + 5L − 7B − 35

⇒ 5L − 7B = 14 ... (Equation 1)

**Case 2:** Length is increased by 4 m and breadth is increased by 5 m.

⇒ New Area = (L + 4)(B + 5)

⇒ LB + 67 = LB + 5L + 4B + 20

⇒ 5L + 4B = 47 ... (Equation 2)

**Calculations:**

⇒ Subtracting Equation 1 from Equation 2:

⇒ (5L + 4B) − (5L − 7B) = 47 − 14

⇒ 11B = 33 ⇒ B = 3 m

⇒ Substituting B = 3 in Equation 1:

⇒ 5L − 7(3) = 14

⇒ 5L − 21 = 14

⇒ 5L = 35 ⇒ L = 7 m

⇒ Original Area = L × B = 7 × 3 = 21 m²

**∴ The correct answer is 21 m².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Area and Perimeter of Rectangle

The area of a rectangle is calculated as Length × Breadth. Its perimeter is given by the formula 2 × (Length + Breadth).

Diagonal of a Rectangle

The diagonal length divides a rectangle into two congruent right-angled triangles. Length of diagonal d = √(L² + B²).

Percentage Change in Area

If the length and breadth of a rectangle are altered by x% and y% respectively, the net percentage change in area is defined by the formula [x + y + (x × y) ÷ 100]%.
</p
